NKE.rationale: NKE exhibits severe fundamental deterioration across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (primary): EPS collapsed 35.2% YoY to $0.35 in Q3 FY2026 on flat revenue, operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M, operating margin compressed to 5.8% from 7.5%, and net margin halved to 4.8% from 9.4% in mid-2025. ROE has fallen from 32.2% to 16.0%. This is not a cyclical dip — it reflects structural margin erosion from tariff exposure (51% Vietnam sourcing, 300bps margin hit), competitive share losses during the prior CEO's wholesale pullback, and declining China revenue. The franchise brand remains world-class but the earnings trajectory is firmly negative with no stabilization visible. Pillar 2 (co-primary): P/E of 28.72x on a severely depressed earnings base is expensive — the market is pricing a recovery that has not materialized. Even the forward 23.4x FY27E multiple (per Seeking Alpha) is rich for a consumer non-durable with no demonstrated top-line growth since FY22. P/B at 4.59x is near range lows but justified by the ROE collapse. Pillar 3 (secondary): The Q4 FY2026 earnings report on June 30, 2026 is a near-term catalyst, but given the trajectory — EPS declining sequentially (0.49→0.53→0.35), negative news sentiment (mean -0.366), Wells Fargo downgrade, and compounding legal/regulatory overhangs (tariff lawsuits, EEOC investigation) — this event is more likely to confirm weakness than trigger a positive re-rating. The risk stack (tariff concentration, China erosion, GLP-1 demand shifts, intensifying competition from Hoka/On/Adidas/New Balance) extends the turnaround timeline materially. Score of -1.0 reflects full alignment: deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation relative to diminished earnings power, and a near-term catalyst more likely to de-rate than re-rate.
